q: A capacitor is used as an electric circuit component to store ____ energy.
e: Capacitors are specifically designed components to store electrical energy within an electric field.

q: The capacitor was originally known as a ____.
e: Historically, the device now known as a capacitor was referred to as a condenser.

q: A capacitor is an electrical device that stores electrical energy in the form of an ____.
e: The energy in a capacitor is stored in the electric field established between its conductors.

q: A capacitor consists of two ____ separated by a small distance.
e: The basic structure of a capacitor involves two conductive plates or surfaces.

q: An ____ is inserted between the conductors of a capacitor.
e: An insulating material, or dielectric, separates the conductors to prevent charge flow between them.

q: Film capacitors are the ones that use plastic film as the ____ medium.
e: Plastic film serves as the insulating dielectric material in film capacitors.

q: Film capacitors are available in nearly any value and working voltages up to ____ V.
e: These capacitors can handle relatively high working voltages, reaching up to 1500 V.

q: Ceramic capacitors are the ones that use ____ as the dielectric material.
e: Ceramic materials are utilized for their stability and insulating properties in these capacitors.

q: Ceramic capacitors are used in ____ circuits such as audio frequency (af) to radio frequency (rf).
e: Their low loss and stability make them ideal for high-frequency applications.

q: Ceramic capacitors are mainly used for high stability performances with low ____.
e: They exhibit minimal energy loss, which is crucial for high-frequency and precision circuits.

q: The capacitance values of ceramic capacitors are stable with respect to the applied voltage, frequency and ____.
e: Ceramic capacitors maintain a consistent capacitance despite fluctuations in temperature.

q: Electrolytic capacitors are the ones that use the ____ layer as the dielectric material.
e: A thin oxide layer formed on the metal anode acts as the dielectric in electrolytic capacitors.

q: There are mainly two types of electrolytic capacitors; tantalum and ____.
e: Aluminum and tantalum are the primary metals used to construct electrolytic capacitors.

q: Electrolytic capacitors are available with working voltages of up to approximately ____ V.
e: These capacitors typically have lower maximum voltage ratings compared to some other types, capping around 500 V.

q: The failure of electrolytic capacitors can be hazardous, resulting in an explosion or ____.
e: Due to their internal chemistry and polarity sensitivity, incorrect usage can lead to dangerous failures.

q: Electrolytic capacitors are used for filtering and smoothing rectified alternating ____.
e: They are heavily used in power supplies to smooth out the ripple in rectified AC voltage.

q: Variable capacitors mostly use ____ as the dielectric medium.
e: Air is commonly used as the dielectric in variable capacitors to allow mechanical adjustment of the plates.

q: The capacitance of a variable capacitor can be ____ adjusted.
e: Rotating the shaft changes the overlapping area of the plates, altering the capacitance.

q: For example, this form of the capacitor is used to set the ____ frequency in tuner devices.
e: Variable capacitors are key components in LC circuits used to tune into specific radio frequencies.

q: Variable capacitors are mostly used in AC circuits especially for high frequency, high power and low ____.
e: Air dielectrics ensure minimal energy loss even at high frequencies and power levels.

q: A supercapacitor (SC), also called an ____, is a high-capacity capacitor with a capacitance value much higher than other capacitors.
e: Supercapacitors and ultracapacitors are synonymous terms for these high-capacity energy storage devices.

q: A supercapacitor bridges the gap between electrolytic capacitors and ____ batteries.
e: They offer higher energy density than standard capacitors and higher power density than rechargeable batteries.

q: A supercapacitor typically stores 10 to ____ times more energy than electrolytic capacitors.
e: Their energy storage capacity vastly exceeds that of conventional electrolytic capacitors.

q: A supercapacitor can accept and deliver charge much ____ than batteries.
e: Because they store energy electrostatically rather than chemically, their charge and discharge rates are extremely rapid.

q: Supercapacitors are used in applications requiring many rapid ____ cycles.
e: They excel in environments where energy must be absorbed and released quickly and repeatedly.

q: In automobiles and trains, supercapacitors are used for ____ braking and short-term energy storage.
e: They capture and store kinetic energy during braking, which can be reused for acceleration.

q: Smaller supercapacitor units are used as power backup for static random-access ____ (SRAM).
e: They provide temporary power to retain data in volatile memory during brief power losses.

q: Film capacitors and ceramic capacitors are ____ capacitors which means that they do not have polarities.
e: These capacitors can be connected in either direction in a DC circuit without risk of damage.

q: Capacitors are used for blocking ____ current after getting fully charged but allow the AC current to pass through it.
e: Once fully charged, a capacitor acts as an open circuit to direct current.

q: Capacitors are used as filters in power supplies and energy-storing devices in electronic ____ units.
e: They rapidly discharge stored energy to produce the bright burst of light needed for photography.

q: Capacitors are also used to tune the ____ of radio receivers.
e: By adjusting capacitance, the resonant frequency of the receiver's tuning circuit is changed.

q: Capacitors are used to eliminate ____ in automobile ignition systems.
e: They absorb the inductive kickback from the ignition coil, protecting the contact points.

q: Capacitors can also be used as the sensor for measuring humidity, fuel levels, mechanical ____, etc.
e: Changes in physical conditions alter the dielectric properties or plate separation, changing the capacitance.

q: A timing capacitor is likely used in any flashing light or regular ____ system.
e: RC circuits utilize the predictable charging time of a capacitor to create timed intervals.

q: When a capacitor is connected to a battery, the two conductors have charges of equal magnitude and ____ signs.
e: One plate accumulates positive charge while the other accumulates an equal amount of negative charge.

q: The magnitude of the charge Q on each conductor is called the ____ of the capacitor.
e: The net charge of the entire capacitor is zero, but 'charge of the capacitor' refers to the magnitude Q on one plate.

q: The potential difference between two conductors of the capacitor is called the potential ____ of the capacitor.
e: This voltage is created by the separation of opposite charges on the two plates.

q: The quantity of charge Q on the capacitor is linearly ____ to the potential difference V between the conductors.
e: As the voltage across the plates increases, the stored charge increases at a constant ratio.

q: This relationship can be written as Q=____, where C is called capacitance of the capacitor.
e: Charge equals capacitance multiplied by the potential difference.

q: The capacitance of a capacitor is defined as the ratio of the charge to the potential ____ of the capacitor.
e: Capacitance measures how much charge is stored per unit of voltage.

q: The capacitance is represented by the equation C=____.
e: This formula defines capacitance mathematically as charge divided by voltage.

q: In the SI system, the unit of capacitance is the ____.
e: The farad is the standard SI derived unit for measuring capacitance.

q: If the potential difference of the capacitor is 1V when it is given a charge 1 C, its capacitance is ____ F.
e: One farad is defined as one coulomb of charge per one volt of potential difference.

q: The unit farad is named in honor of Michael ____.
e: The unit commemorates the English scientist Michael Faraday for his contributions to electromagnetism.

q: The farad is a very ____ unit of capacitance.
e: In practical electronics, one farad is an enormous amount of capacitance, so sub-multiples are used.

q: In practice, typical devices have capacitances ranging from microfarad ($\mu F$) to ____.
e: Most standard electronic circuits utilize capacitors in the microfarad, nanofarad, or picofarad range.

q: 1 microfarad ($\mu F$) = ____ F.
e: The prefix 'micro' denotes a factor of one millionth.

q: 1 nanofarad (nF) = ____ F.
e: The prefix 'nano' denotes a factor of one billionth.

q: 1 picofarad (pF) = ____ F.
e: The prefix 'pico' denotes a factor of one trillionth.

q: When the charge on the capacitor is increased, the potential difference also increases ____.
e: Because C is constant, V must increase in direct proportion to Q.

q: When the charge on a capacitor is increased, its capacitance remains ____.
e: Capacitance is a physical property determined by geometry and dielectric, not by the applied voltage or charge.

q: Although the capacitance does not depend on Q and V, it depends on the size, shape, and the nature of the ____ between the two conductors.
e: The dielectric material's permittivity directly influences the overall capacitance.

q: The amount of charge given to a conductor to change its potential by one unit is called the electric ____ of the conductor.
e: This concept applies to isolated conductors as well as two-plate capacitors.

q: A ____ capacitor is the simplest capacitor.
e: It consists of two flat, parallel conducting plates and serves as the foundational model for capacitance.

q: A parallel-plate capacitor consists of two parallel metal plates separated by air or other ____ material.
e: The space between the plates must be filled with a dielectric to prevent charge transfer.

q: The surface charge density on each plate is defined as charge per unit surface ____.
e: Surface charge density ($\sigma$) is calculated by dividing the total charge Q by the plate area A.

q: If the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor are very close together, the electric field between the plates is ____.
e: A uniform electric field exists in the central region when the plate separation is much smaller than the plate dimensions.

q: Because the electric field between the plates is uniform, the magnitude of the potential difference V between the plates equals ____.
e: Voltage is the product of the uniform electric field strength and the distance between the plates.

q: For a given insulating material the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is directly proportional to the ____ of its plates.
e: Larger plates provide more surface area to store separated charges.

q: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the ____ of the plates.
e: Bringing the plates closer together increases the attractive force between opposite charges, allowing more charge to be stored for a given voltage.

q: The permittivity $\epsilon$ of an insulating material is related to that of a vacuum $\epsilon_0$ as $\epsilon = K$ ____.
e: The absolute permittivity is the product of the dielectric constant and the permittivity of free space.

q: Here K is the ____ constant or the relative permittivity of the insulating material.
e: The dielectric constant is a dimensionless number indicating how much a material increases capacitance compared to a vacuum.

q: The permittivity of vacuum $\epsilon_0$ is approximately ____ $C^2 N^{-1} m^{-2}$.
e: This is a fundamental physical constant representing the capability of a vacuum to permit electric field lines.

q: For a vacuum K=____ and for other insulating materials K>1.
e: A vacuum serves as the baseline reference, so its relative permittivity is exactly 1.

q: The dielectric constant of an insulating material is the ratio of its permittivity to that of ____.
e: It compares a material's ability to store electrical energy against the baseline of empty space.

q: The ratio of the capacitance with an insulating material to the capacitance with a ____ between the conductors is called the dielectric constant.
e: This provides a practical way to measure K by comparing the same capacitor with and without the dielectric.

q: When a charged capacitor is disconnected from a battery and a dielectric is inserted, the potential difference is found to ____.
e: The dielectric polarizes, creating an internal electric field that opposes the original field, thus lowering the voltage.

q: Since the charge Q of a disconnected capacitor does not change when a dielectric is inserted, it indicates that the capacitance ____.
e: Because C = Q/V, a decrease in V while Q remains constant results in a higher capacitance.

q: Insulating materials have values of dielectric constant K greater than ____.
e: All physical dielectric materials increase capacitance compared to a vacuum, meaning K > 1.

q: A dielectric provides an increase in ____, an increase in maximum operating voltage, and possible mechanical support.
e: Inserting a dielectric multiplies the original vacuum capacitance by the factor K.

q: A dielectric increases the maximum operating ____ of a capacitor even though the physical size doesn't change.
e: Dielectric materials generally have higher dielectric strength than air, preventing electrical breakdown at higher voltages.

q: The dielectric may be able to withstand a larger electric ____ between the plates than air.
e: This prevents arcing or sparking across the gap when high voltages are applied.

q: A capacitor stores electrical energy in the form of an electric ____.
e: The energy is physically located in the stressed electric field between the charged plates.

q: When the capacitor is charged, the process can be viewed as the apparent ____ of charge between two conductors.
e: Electrons are moved from one plate to the other, leaving one positive and the other negative.

q: The charge has been transferred from a conductor at lower potential to a conductor at ____ potential.
e: Work must be done to push positive charge against the electric field toward the higher potential plate.

q: The energy stored by the capacitor can be analyzed from the ____ graph.
e: Plotting charge against voltage yields a straight line where the area under the curve represents work done.

q: The work done in charging the capacitor is given by the shaded ____ under the curve.
e: The integral of V with respect to Q gives the total energy stored.

q: This work done is equal to ____ which is the energy stored by the capacitor.
e: The area of the triangle on a Q-V graph is one-half base times height.

q: Before a capacitor is charged, the potential difference between its two conductors is ____.
e: An uncharged capacitor has no separation of charge, hence no voltage.

q: Suppose that after charging, each conductor receives a charge of ____ Q and the potential difference is V.
e: Both plates hold the exact same amount of charge, just with opposite signs.

q: The average potential difference of the capacitor before and after it is charged is $\frac{0+V}{2}$ which equals ____.
e: Because the voltage rises linearly with charge, the average voltage during charging is half the final voltage.

q: This amount of work is, in fact, the electrical ____ stored by the capacitor.
e: The work done by the battery is conserved as potential energy in the electric field.

q: Therefore the energy of the capacitor is ____.
e: Total work equals total charge multiplied by the average voltage during the charging process.

q: Since C=Q/V, the energy W of the capacitor can be expressed as W = ____.
e: Substituting Q = CV into the energy equation yields this common formula.

q: Placing a ____ in the charging circuit slows down the charging process.
e: Resistance limits the current flow, increasing the time required to charge the capacitor.

q: The greater the values of resistance and capacitance, the ____ it takes to charge the capacitor.
e: Both higher resistance and higher capacitance increase the RC time constant.

q: The product of the resistance R and the capacitance C is called the time ____ of the process.
e: The time constant ($\tau$) represents the time required to charge the capacitor to about 63.2% of its final voltage.

q: The time constant of an RC circuit is measured in ____.
e: Ohms multiplied by farads mathematically reduces to the SI unit of time, seconds.

q: The voltage rises with time according to the equation $V_c = $ ____.
e: This exponential equation describes the asymptotic approach of the capacitor voltage toward the supply voltage.

q: The voltage of the capacitor falls off with time according to the equation $V_c = $ ____.
e: This equation models the exponential decay of voltage as the capacitor discharges through a resistor.

q: Several capacitors can be ____ together to be used in a variety of applications.
e: Combining capacitors allows for custom capacitance values not available as single components.

q: There are two types of combination namely; parallel and ____.
e: These are the two fundamental ways to wire multiple components in a circuit.

q: In a parallel combination, all the capacitors have the same potential ____.
e: Because their terminals are connected to the same two common nodes, the voltage across each is identical.

q: When capacitors are connected in parallel, they carry ____ amounts of charges.
e: If the capacitances are different, the charge stored on each ($Q=CV$) will also differ.

q: If Q is the total charge on three capacitors in parallel, then Q = ____.
e: The total charge supplied by the battery is distributed among the parallel branches.

q: We can replace the three capacitors in parallel with a ____ capacitor provided it has the same total charge Q.
e: An equivalent capacitor simplifies circuit analysis by behaving identically to the entire network.

q: The equivalent capacitance of capacitors connected in parallel is the ____ of the individual capacitances.
e: Connecting in parallel effectively increases the total surface area of the plates.

q: The equivalent capacitance C of the parallel combination of n identical capacitors, each of capacitance $C_1$, is C = ____.
e: Adding identical capacitors in parallel simply multiplies the single capacitance value by the number of components.

q: In a series combination, the negatively charged plate of one capacitor is connected to the ____ charged plate of the other.
e: This daisy-chain connection forces the same charge displacement through the entire string.

q: Since the capacitors are connected in series each capacitor has the same ____.
e: Electrostatic induction ensures that the exact same magnitude of charge accumulates on every plate in the series string.

q: When capacitors are connected in series, they have ____ potential differences.
e: Unless the capacitances are identical, the voltage divides unequally across the components ($V=Q/C$).

q: Suppose that V is the ____ potential difference of the series capacitor combination.
e: The sum of the individual voltage drops equals the total applied voltage.

q: We can replace the three capacitors in series with an ____ capacitor.
e: This single component represents the overall capacitive effect of the series network.

q: When connected in series, the ____ of the equivalent capacitance is the sum of the reciprocals of their individual capacitances.
e: This mathematical relationship arises because voltages add while charge remains constant.

q: The equivalent capacitance $C_s$ of the series combination of n identical capacitors, each of capacitance C, is $C_s = $ ____.
e: Placing identical capacitors in series divides the total capacitance by the number of components.
